title: The human-authorship halo: attribution bias in literary style evaluation by humans and AI
abstract: arXiv:2510.08831v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: As AI writing tools become widespread, we need to understand how both humans and machines evaluate literary style, a domain where objective standards are elusive and judgments are inherently subjective. We conducted controlled experiments using Raymond Queneau's Exercises in Style (1947) to measure attribution bias across evaluators. Study 1 compared human participants (N=556) and AI models (N=13) evaluating literary passages from Queneau versus GPT-4-generated versions under three conditions: blind, accurately labeled, and counterfactually labeled. Study 2 tested bias generalization across a 14x14 matrix of AI evaluators and creators. Both studies revealed systematic pro-human attribution bias. Humans showed +13.7 percentage point (pp) bias (Cohen's h = 0.28, 95% CI: 0.19-0.37), while AI models showed +34.3 percentage point bias (h = 0.70, 95% CI: 0.62-0.78), a 2.5-fold stronger effect (P<0.001). Study 2 confirmed this bias operates

translated_title: 人类作者光环：人类与AI在文学风格评价中的归因偏差
translated_abstract: 随着AI写作工具的普及，我们需要理解人类和机器如何评估文学风格——这是一个客观标准难以确立、判断本质上主观的领域。我们使用雷蒙·格诺的《风格练习》（1947）进行了受控实验，以测量不同评价者之间的归因偏差。研究1比较了人类参与者（N=556）和AI模型（N=13）在三种条件下（盲评、准确标注和反事实标注）对格诺的文学段落与GPT-4生成版本的评估。研究2在14×14的AI评价者与创作者矩阵中测试了偏差的泛化性。两项研究都揭示了系统性的亲人类归因偏差。人类表现出+13.7个百分点的偏差（Cohen's h = 0.28，95% CI: 0.19-0.37），而AI模型表现出+34.3个百分点的偏差（h = 0.70，95% CI: 0.62-0.78），效应强度是人类的2.5倍（P<0.001）。研究2证实了这种偏差的运作机制。
tldr: 该研究通过受控实验首次系统量化了人类与AI在文学风格评价中的“亲人类作者”归因偏差，发现AI模型的这种偏差比人类强2.5倍。
en_tdlr: This study systematically quantifies pro-human attribution bias in literary style evaluation by both humans and AI, finding that AI models exhibit a 2.5-fold stronger bias than humans.
